response.sql: WITH customer_orders AS (SELECT c.customer_id, c.gender, COUNT(o.order_id) as num_orders FROM Customers c LEFT JOIN Orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id WHERE c.gender IS NOT NULL GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.gender), gender_stats AS (SELECT customer_id, gender, num_orders, SUM(num_orders) OVER (PARTITION BY gender) as total_by_gender FROM customer_orders), shares_and_avg AS (SELECT customer_id, gender, num_orders, CAST(num_orders AS DECIMAL(19,4)) / CAST(total_by_gender AS DECIMAL(19,4)) as share, AVG(CAST(num_orders AS DECIMAL(19,4)) / CAST(total_by_gender AS DECIMAL(19,4))) OVER (PARTITION BY gender) as avg_share FROM gender_stats) SELECT customer_id, gender, num_orders, share, share - avg_share as gap_above_average FROM shares_and_avg WHERE share > avg_share ORDER BY gap_above_average DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 10

assumptions.assumption: The average share for each gender is calculated across all customers of that gender (including those with zero orders), not just among customers with at least one order. This interpretation aligns with the request to consider 'all customers, including those who have never placed an order.'
